weeks.theme: Shared norms for clear English in a KR–JP merger

scenarios.title: Set working agreements for mixed-language meetings
scenarios.situation: Kick off the first joint squad meeting to agree on how we speak, capture notes, and make decisions in English.
targetPhrases: Let's speak slowly and avoid idioms.
One person at a time, please.
Can we agree on a single source of truth?
Let's timebox this to five minutes.
We'll capture owners and due dates.
scenarios.successLooksLike: The team agrees on simple-English norms, turn-taking, and note-taking with owners and dates; people repeat back key decisions before moving on.

scenarios.title: Clarify ambiguous terms across KR/JP contexts
scenarios.situation: A term like "service" or "campaign" means different things to each company; align on a definition.
targetPhrases: When you say X, do you mean…?
Let's define X as… for this project.
I might be misunderstanding—do you mean…?
Could you give a concrete example?
Let's document this in the glossary.
scenarios.successLooksLike: People surface and resolve different interpretations quickly and record a shared definition without side debates.

scenarios.title: Polite repair when you miss something
scenarios.situation: You didn't catch a colleague's point in English and need them to rephrase without slowing the meeting too much.
targetPhrases: Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?
Could you rephrase that another way?
Let me repeat what I heard… is that right?
I lost the thread—what’s the key point?
Can we park details and capture an action?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Requests for clarification are brief and respectful; restatements show correct understanding and the meeting stays on track.

scenarios.title: 45‑second standup update
scenarios.situation: Daily standup with mixed KR/JP team where time is tight.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Updates are under 45 seconds, follow the format, and make blockers and asks explicit so others can help.

scenarios.title: Clear Slack/Teams update across time zones
scenarios.situation: Posting an async update so the other office knows progress while you sleep.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Posts include context, owner, date, and a clear ask so no follow-up is needed to act.

scenarios.title: Handover at end of day
scenarios.situation: Passing an in-progress task to a counterpart before sign-off.
scenarios.successLooksLike: The receiver can continue work without pinging for basics; handovers get a quick acknowledgment.

scenarios.title: Clarify acceptance criteria
scenarios.situation: User story is vague; align on what "done" looks like.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Stories have clear acceptance criteria with examples; no rework due to misinterpretation.

scenarios.title: Split oversized stories
scenarios.situation: Break down a large item to deliver earlier value.
targetPhrases: Can we slice by user flow?
Let’s ship A first, then B.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Work is split into smaller increments with a rationale and identified dependencies.

scenarios.title: Push back on scope creep
scenarios.situation: Stakeholder adds last-minute asks during grooming.
targetPhrases: Given the deadline, adding X means dropping Y.
Can we defer this to next sprint?
What is the actual user impact?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Team negotiates scope trade-offs calmly and documents a clear decision and next steps.

scenarios.title: Engineer requests spec clarification
scenarios.situation: Requirements are unclear; avoid building the wrong thing.
targetPhrases: I need a concrete example of…
What does success look like in numbers?
Can we align on error handling?
Let’s capture this as an action item.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Questions lead to specific, testable requirements; decisions are captured with owners and dates.

scenarios.title: Ops raises operational constraints
scenarios.situation: Operations flags risk with current plan (SLA, staffing, support hours).
targetPhrases: Can we pilot with a subset?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Plan is adjusted to respect ops constraints, with a clear mitigation and pilot where needed.

scenarios.title: Actionable spec comment in English
scenarios.situation: Leave a clear comment on a spec or PR that moves work forward.
targetPhrases: Could you clarify X by adding…
scenarios.successLooksLike: Comments are polite, specific, and lead to timely updates without back-and-forth.

weeks.theme: Roadmap and OKR alignment across companies

scenarios.title: Explain a trade‑off to leadership
scenarios.situation: Present options with impact, effort, and risk to get a decision.
targetPhrases: We can deliver X by Y if we drop Z.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Leaders understand options quickly and make a decision in the meeting.

scenarios.title: Negotiate priorities between KR/JP platforms
scenarios.situation: Two similar features compete for resources; seek a shared plan.
targetPhrases: Can we align on a joint MVP?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Teams agree on a joint MVP and phased plan tied to a shared metric.

scenarios.title: Set quarterly OKRs in simple English
scenarios.situation: Define outcomes everyone can understand and measure.
scenarios.successLooksLike: OKRs are concise, measurable, and owned; both teams interpret them the same way.

scenarios.title: Join an incident bridge call
scenarios.situation: Cross-company outage; speak clearly under pressure.
targetPhrases: We need to roll back/disable feature flag.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Updates are crisp, roles are clear, and actions happen without repeating requests.

scenarios.title: On‑call handover
scenarios.situation: Shift change across time zones during an incident.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Incoming on-call takes over smoothly; no gaps or duplicated work.

scenarios.title: Write a blameless postmortem summary
scenarios.situation: Summarize timeline, root cause, and follow-ups for a mixed audience.
targetPhrases: Action items with owners and dates…
scenarios.successLooksLike: Summary is readable by non-specialists and leads to concrete prevention actions.

scenarios.title: Map data fields and definitions
scenarios.situation: Align schema and field meaning to merge two systems.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Mappings are unambiguous with examples; edge cases and assumptions are documented.

scenarios.title: Agree on API contract
scenarios.situation: Define request/response, errors, and versioning.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Both sides can implement independently; contract covers errors and performance.

scenarios.title: Plan cutover and rollback
scenarios.situation: Choose a safe migration window and fallback.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Cutover plan has criteria, timing, and comms; rollback is tested and owned.

scenarios.title: Handoff test cases
scenarios.situation: QA shares what to test and how to reproduce issues.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Test cases are executable without pinging QA; sign-off criteria are known.

scenarios.title: Triage a blocker bug
scenarios.situation: Decide whether to fix now or defer.
targetPhrases: Risk of shipping with bug is…
scenarios.successLooksLike: Team agrees quickly on action with owner and timeline; release risk is explicit.

scenarios.title: Coordinate a feature-flagged release
scenarios.situation: Staged rollout with monitoring and rollback.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Rollout steps are clear; support and ops know what to expect and when.

scenarios.title: Resolve ownership confusion
scenarios.situation: Two teams think the other owns a task.
targetPhrases: I propose ownership sits with… because…
scenarios.successLooksLike: Ownership and dates are resolved in one conversation and recorded.

scenarios.title: Reduce tension about rework
scenarios.situation: A team is frustrated about changing requirements.
targetPhrases: Here’s what we can keep vs change.
Let’s focus on impact, not blame.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Tone stays professional; both sides agree on a path forward and follow-up time.

scenarios.title: Push back on an unrealistic deadline
scenarios.situation: A leader requests delivery that risks quality.
targetPhrases: With current scope, the earliest date is…
We can meet the date if we drop X.
scenarios.successLooksLike: A realistic plan is accepted, or trade-offs are documented with leader approval.

scenarios.title: Propose a combined workflow
scenarios.situation: Merge two different ways of working into one lightweight process.
scenarios.successLooksLike: The proposal is understood and a small pilot with owners and dates is approved.

scenarios.title: Document the single source of truth
scenarios.situation: Decide where roadmaps, specs, and decisions live.
targetPhrases: Our single source of truth is…
scenarios.successLooksLike: Everyone knows where to find current docs; old sources are deprecated with a date.

scenarios.title: Agree on meeting hygiene
scenarios.situation: Standardize agendas, notes, and action tracking.
targetPhrases: Owner and due date for each action.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Meetings start on time, end with clear actions, and notes are posted within 24 hours.

scenarios.title: Align with an external vendor in English
scenarios.situation: Kickoff call to clarify SOW and interfaces.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Vendor repeats back scope and dates correctly; change and escalation paths are written.

scenarios.title: Leadership progress update
scenarios.situation: Brief update to execs who have 10 minutes.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Leaders quickly grasp status and make or confirm needed decisions in the meeting.

scenarios.title: Respond to a scope change request
scenarios.situation: Stakeholder asks for new features mid‑sprint; provide an impact assessment.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Stakeholder chooses an option based on a clear, concise impact summary.

scenarios.title: Write a clear how‑to
scenarios.situation: Create a step‑by‑step guide another team can follow without help.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Another team completes the task using only the guide; no clarifying pings needed.

scenarios.title: Record a crisp handover
scenarios.situation: End-of-project handover of systems/processes.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Receiving team confirms they have what they need and acknowledges ownership.

scenarios.title: Run a brief retrospective
scenarios.situation: Close the program with a focus on improving cross-company English collaboration.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Team agrees on 2–3 concrete behavior changes and assigns owners and dates.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Status updates and meeting talk are short, structured, and easy to act on.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: In a sample of 50 standup updates, 80% follow the Yesterday/Today/Blockers format and stay under 45 seconds.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Meeting notes consistently show clear owners and dates so work moves without chasing people.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: Across four weeks, 90% of meeting notes reviewed include action items with an owner and due date.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Cross-team handoffs don’t require extra back-and-forth to understand what to do next.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: Compared to month 1, reduce clarification messages on handovers by 30% in months 2–3 (sample Slack/Teams threads).

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Leadership and vendor updates lead to decisions in the room (not after many emails).
successCriteria.measurableProxy: In a sample of 10 leader/vendor updates, at least 8 end with a documented decision and next step within the meeting or same day.

kickoffMessage.en: Welcome to the KR–JP Integration English Program. Over the next 12 weeks, we’ll use practical scenarios from our merger work—incident bridges, backlog grooming, roadmap alignment, vendor calls, and more—to build a simple, shared way of working in English. Our norms: speak slowly, avoid idioms, confirm understanding, and always capture owners and dates. It’s okay to ask "Can you say that another way?" or "Let me repeat what I heard." Clarity beats perfect grammar. In mixed groups, default to English so everyone can participate. Thank you for committing to clear, respectful communication.
kickoffMessage.ko: KR–JP 통합 영어 프로그램에 오신 것을 환영합니다. 앞으로 12주 동안, 사고 대응 브리지 콜, 백로그 그루밍, 로드맵 정렬, 벤더 미팅 등 실제 통합 업무 상황을 사용하여 영어로 단순하고 공유 가능한 업무 방식을 만들겠습니다. 우리의 기본 규칙: 천천히 말하기, 관용구 피하기, 이해 확인하기, 그리고 반드시 담당자와 마감일을 기록하기. "다른 표현으로 말씀해 주실 수 있나요?", "제가 이해한 바를 다시 말해 보겠습니다"라고 말해도 괜찮습니다. 완벽한 문법보다 명확함이 더 중요합니다. 혼합 팀에서는 모두가 참여할 수 있도록 기본적으로 영어를 사용합시다. 명확하고 존중하는 소통에 함께해 주셔서 감사합니다.
